standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the computational core: conditions (2), (4), (5) are equivalent because the first Fitting ideal is generated by the (n-1)-minors of the Jacobian matrix.

standard_prerequisites.name: Nodal algebras and the delta-invariant
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, Lemmas lemma-nodal-algebraic, lemma-multicross-algebra and lemma-2-branches-delta-1
standard_prerequisites.use: Identifies condition (1) over an algebraically closed base with the nondegenerate quadric xy, and condition (6) with separability, reducedness, delta-invariant 1 and 2 geometric branches.

core_obligations: Over an algebraically closed field (proof lines 4411-4440): (1) = (3) is trivial, (1) = (2) because the only nondegenerate quadric in two variables is xy up to coordinate change, (1) = (6) is lemma-multicross-algebra, and (2), (4), (5) are equivalent via the Jacobian presentation and lemma-fitting-ideal applied to the completed immersion X -> A^n_k.

Separability descent to arbitrary k (proof lines 4443-4473): the Fitting-ideal subscheme Z commutes with field extension (divisors-lemma-base-change-and-fitting-ideal-omega); if (1) or (3) holds, Z_kbar has an isolated multiplicity-1 point, so Z is geometrically reduced at x and kappa(x)/k is separable.

Transfer of (4), (5) across the flat local map O_{X,x} -> O_{X_kbar, xbar} (proof lines 4476-4500), and conversely (5) implies (3) by geometric reducedness of Z over kbar; this closes (1), (3), (4), (5).

Bridge to (2) = (6) (proof lines 4503-4530): equality of geometric branch counts under base change, the delta-invariant inequality with its strictness argument (delta = 0 would make O_{X,x} a DVR, unibranch), and Varieties, Lemma varieties-lemma-geometrically-normal-in-codim-1 via lemma-2-branches-delta-1 give the reverse inclusion.
proof_roadmap: Do the algebraically closed case first: quadric normal form, multicross equivalence, Fitting presentation.
For arbitrary k, deduce separability of kappa(x)/k from the isolated multiplicity-1 point of the base-changed Fitting subscheme.
Move (4) and (5) across the flat local map to the geometric fibre and back, closing the circle (1), (3), (4), (5).
Use lemma-2-branches-delta-1 to identify (2) with (6) and connect both to the closed circle via the delta-invariant inequality and its reverse.
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives six equivalent characterizations of a node (statement lines 4390-4408). The proof (lines 4410-4518) is a two-stage argument: first the complete classification over an algebraically closed field through the nondegenerate quadric xy and the Fitting-ideal presentation of Omega, then a genuine descent to arbitrary fields in which separability of kappa(x)/k, geometric reducedness of the Fitting subscheme, flat transfer of depth, and the delta-invariant inequality with its DVR contradiction each carry weight. H2: every individual step is a reference application or a short computation, but the equivalence web must be assembled in the right order and the field-extension bookkeeping is not routine.
